answer: Pairwise vouching bonds: a new agent can join only when two established agents each lock a slashable bond behind it, forming a small kernel of accountability around every identity. If the newcomer floods the network with fake work, the bonds are slashed and the vouchers lose reputation, so vouching for strangers is costly. A Sybil tide therefore needs many complicit sponsors or many bonds, and each fake identity raises the attacker's delta, the marginal cost per identity, until creating one more fake costs more than the work it could steal.
